turns.content:
hey thanks for taking a look at this with me. so i'm looking at the benefits handbook for my company's open enrollment and there's this section that i want to sanity-check with you real quick. i'll just quote it:

"Section 4.2: The Health Risk Assessment questionnaire must be finalized in the portal by October 31. Biometric screening results from an in-network provider or on-site screening event may be submitted via physician attestation form through December 1 for discount application starting January 1."

so my annual physical with dr chen is nov 14... i'm reading this as the biometric submission window (dec 1) is separate from the online assessment cutoff (oct 31). meaning i can still get the screening done at my physical and submit it after october, right? just want to make sure i'm not missing something.

The quoted language treats the two items as separate deadlines.

**HRA:** The questionnaire must be finished in the portal by October 31. A November 14 physical does not meet that cutoff.

**Biometrics:** Results from an in-network provider or an on-site event may be submitted on a physician attestation form through December 1, for a discount that starts January 1. A November 14 visit falls inside that window.

What this snippet does **not** establish: whether both pieces are required for the discount; whether Dr. Chen counts as in-network; whether that office will complete the attestation form; or whether another handbook section, portal rule, or HR FAQ adds conditions.

Complete the portal HRA by October 31 if you need that piece. For the physical, confirm in-network status and that they will submit the attestation by December 1.

ok that makes sense. i figured the hra and biometrics were separate deadlines but nice to have it confirmed. so i just need to make sure the hra is done by oct 31 in the portal and then the physical on nov 14 gives me plenty of time for the attestation by dec 1.

one thing though — what exactly is a physician attestation form? is that something dr chen's office would be familiar with or is it a specific company form i need to bring?

The handbook line only says results **may be submitted via physician attestation form**. It does not define the form, who issues it, or whether the office already has it.

In employer wellness programs, that phrase usually means a **company- or vendor-specific form** (not a standard medical record) on which the clinician or staff records biometric values (for example blood pressure, BMI, cholesterol, glucose) and signs that the screening was done. Many primary-care offices have seen similar forms from other employers; they will not automatically know *your* company’s version or how to file it.

Treat it as something **you obtain and bring or upload**, unless the portal or HR says the office can pull it themselves.

**Do this before November 14:** In the same portal as the HRA, or in the rest of the handbook / benefits FAQ, find the attestation form or the exact submission path (paper, fax, upload). If it is not there, ask HR or the wellness vendor for the form and the deadline/method. Then ask Dr. Chen’s office whether they complete employer biometric attestation forms and whether they need the blank form at the visit.

Confirm Dr. Chen is in-network for this screening, as the quoted rule requires that (or an on-site event).

ok got it. so the hra is a separate thing i need to knock out by oct 31 in the portal, then the physical nov 14 gives me time for the attestation by dec 1. makes sense.

but the handbook also has a section 4.3 that lists what counts as a qualified biometric screening... it says "standard fasting lipid panel and glucose" plus bp and bmi. does a routine annual physical with those labs automatically satisfy that, or do they want some specific employer-branded form filled out?

Section 4.3 (as you quoted) defines **which measurements** count. Section 4.2 still defines **how they must be turned in**.

A routine physical that includes a fasting lipid panel, glucose, blood pressure, and BMI does **not** automatically complete the requirement. Those results still have to be submitted on the physician attestation form by December 1. The handbook language you quoted does not say lab work in the chart, or a normal physical note, is enough by itself.

Whether that form is employer- or vendor-branded is not stated in the lines you quoted. Treat it as a form you get from the portal, handbook, HR, or wellness vendor and bring or send to the office, unless those sources say otherwise.

**Unknowns that matter:** the full text of 4.3 (other rules, alternate submission paths); whether Dr. Chen is in-network for this screening; whether the office will complete that form.

Before November 14: get the attestation form and submission instructions; tell the office you need a **fasting** lipid panel and glucose plus BP and BMI recorded on that form; confirm they will sign and that you can file it by December 1. The HRA in the portal by October 31 remains a separate deadline.

hmm ok that all makes sense. i guess i was just wondering if section 4.5 says anything about when the credit actually starts — like does it hit the january 1 payroll or is there some retroactive thing if paperwork ends up late?

I do not have Section 4.5. You have not quoted it, so I cannot say what it covers.

The only timing rule in the text you provided is Section 4.2: attestation through December 1 **for discount application starting January 1**. That line does not say the credit is retroactive, does not mention payroll dates, and does not say what happens if the form is late.

Paste the full text of 4.5 (and any nearby sentence on late or incomplete submissions) if you want that checked the same way.

yeah ok that's fair, i haven't quoted 4.5 yet. let me pull it up... it says "Section 4.5: The wellness discount will be applied to the first payroll of January following the plan year in which all requirements are met. No retroactive adjustment will be made for incomplete submissions." so that confirms no retroactivity, just jan 1 start if everything's in by dec 1. sounds straightforward

Section 4.5, as quoted, confirms **no retroactive adjustment** if submissions are incomplete. It does **not** by itself confirm “January 1 if everything is in by December 1.”

What 4.5 actually says:
- The discount is applied to the **first payroll of January following the plan year in which all requirements are met**.
- Incomplete submissions get **no retroactive adjustment**.

December 1 and “starting January 1” are from **4.2**, not 4.5. 4.5 also says **first payroll of January**, which may not be the January 1 calendar date.

The phrase **“following the plan year in which all requirements are met”** is not defined in the lines you quoted. If the plan year is the calendar year and you finish in 2026, a literal reading could point to January **after that plan year ends**, not January 2026. That would conflict with 4.2’s “starting January 1.” Those two sections only line up if “plan year” is defined so that meeting the Oct 31 / Dec 1 cutoffs counts as meeting requirements **for** the January that 4.2 names.

**Unknowns that settle it:** the handbook’s definition of plan year; any sentence that ties 4.2’s January 1 to 4.5’s first January payroll.

Paste the plan-year definition (or the 4.2–4.5 cross-reference) if you want that mismatch checked. Until then, treat 4.5 as: complete **all** required pieces (HRA by Oct 31 and attestation by Dec 1, plus anything else listed) or there is no catch-up on later paychecks.
